Both halves resolved 2026-08-23; exoplasim/notes/physics-filter-stability.md carries the evidence.

THE BIAS HALF IS REFUTED, by the arm built to test it. The claim was that denergy26 carries the filter to the first power and denergy27 carries it squared, so 26-27 could not vanish under a nontrivial filter however well the core conserves. With the filter OFF, f = 1, both terms carry the same weight by construction and the bias term is exactly zero -- and the residual is the LARGEST of the whole grid, 0.5575 against 0.1204 for kappa 8 at the same step. Removing the bias raises the residual 4.6x where the hypothesis needs it to fall to zero. Confirmed across nine further cells: the residual grows monotonically as the filter weakens at every timestep.

What the dependences say instead is truncation error. It scales with the timestep, ratios of 0.60 at dt 30 and 0.38-0.41 at dt 22.5 against linear's 0.667 and 0.500, consistent across kappa 8, 4 and 2. So water-and-energy-closure.md's attribution to the semi-implicit step stands, and its number is not a constant of the model: 0.31 W/m2 is what this timestep and this filter cost. Eight-orbit arms confirm the short windows to within 2%.

THE UNBOOKED HALF IS BOUNDED, by an identity that runs the wrong way for it. Nothing books the filter's KE removal -- mkdheat covers Rayleigh friction and biharmonic diffusion, fluxmod the surface and vertical-diffusion terms, neither knows the filter exists -- and the filter preserves n=0 exactly so only the quadratic quantity is exposed. The kinetic-energy steady-state identity is what would find it, and a stronger filter removes more, so the gap must WIDEN with kappa if the filter is the missing term. It NARROWS: -0.013 to -0.000 at kappa 8, rising through +0.007 at kappa 2 to +0.039 with the filter OFF, where the filter's dissipation is identically zero and there is nothing to book.

At the adopted kappa 8 the identity closes to within 0.013 W/m2 against a conversion of about 2.1, six tenths of a percent. The term is real in principle and below what this instrument can see at production settings, so the row closes on the bound rather than on an mkdheat implementation.

REOPEN IF: the identity stops closing at the adopted kappa, or a rung's KE conversion grows enough that six tenths of a percent is worth chasing.

THE FILTER BUYS TIMESTEP, so a filter strength and a timestep are one decision. Without the filter the model traps in the shortwave on the first radiation call at 45 minutes and runs at 22.5, and the requirement STRENGTHENS up the ladder: unfiltered, T42 runs at dt 30 and T170 needs dt 10. That is upstream's stated reason for filtering, measured rather than quoted -- a finer grid resolves sharper gradients off the same orography while a scale-free filter keeps cutting the same fraction.

KAPPA 8 AT EVERY RUNG, and it is not a compromise because it wins on both axes. Against kappa 4, 2, 1 and off it takes the longest stable step at every rung tested AND gives the smallest adiabatic non-conservation -- 0.3147 W/m2 at dt 45 against 0.3460, 0.4020, 0.6574 and a trap. What it costs is spectrum, which is the only reason not to go stronger: f is scale-free in n/NTRU with its half-power point at 0.737, so a stronger filter takes more of every rung's spectrum for a benefit nothing has measured. Nothing above kappa 8 was tested.

MARTICORENA ET AL. (1997) IS WHY THEY DIFFER, and it says so directly: Saharan
lakes fed by streams "loaded with detritic sediments became clayey plains with
SMOOTH SURFACES", while "paleolakes, fed by superficial gypseous water, became
EMBOSSED TOPOGRAPHY, sensitive to weathering", with sebkha surfaces varying
"depending on their salt content and on the experienced periods of drying and
moistening". A clastic playa and an evaporite pan are a smooth surface and a
rough, more variable one.

MACKINNON ET AL. (2004) MEASURED THE ROUGH ONE. Their site 208 is a playa
carrying `saltpush` -- "salt push-ups or ridges created by expanding salt and
clay crusts on playa surfaces", 2 cm high, 5 cm apart -- and it is the strongest
sheltering species there, threshold friction velocity ratio 0.75 against 0.98
and 0.99 for the bushes beside it. Its aerodynamically derived z0 is 0.014 cm
over a 0.0053 to 0.039 cm range. That is the evaporite central value and bracket
unchanged.

PRIGENT ET AL. (2005) CARRIES THE SMOOTH ONE. The Bodele and Chott Djerid
depressions, the Sahara's strongest dust sources, "could have been lakes during
former wet climate periods, allowing accumulation of sediments. For those
regions it can be expected that the surface is relatively smooth, with low
roughness parameters." Their convention for active dust sources is 0.001 cm and
their sand-desert boundary is 0.02 cm, which set the ends.

goes as 1/ln(z/z0) and it is ln(z0) that averages. The arms are now fields, not
scalars, so a cell of pure playa and a cell of pure evaporite sit at different
roughnesses within one arm.

read_atmos_restart reads nlat, nlon, nlev and nrsp before any array read and refuses a mismatch by name, printing both geometries and pointing at convert_restart.py. denergyfix is in the restart: put_restart_real in epilog, get_restart_real in read_atmos_restart under the lowered nexcheck so a restart written before this reads as zero. A segment now starts on the previous segment's converged correction instead of at zero, which ends both halves of the finding -- the 2*ntspd uncorrected steps at every segment boundary, and any run shorter than one window applying no correction at all, the 20-step transform gates included.

The three window accumulators (denergyacc, nenergyacc, nenergywin) are DELIBERATELY NOT saved, and this is the part that is a decision rather than a fix. The first step out of a restart carries a start-up transient of order 250 W/m2 and the design discards the first window for exactly that reason; splicing a partial window across a segment boundary would feed that transient into the previous segment's average, which is the failure the windowing exists to avoid. A segment therefore applies the carried correction from step one and measures its own clean window before changing it.

DSMAX is now surface.glaciers.max_snow_depth_m in config/planet.yaml, declared as -1 (landmod's own no-limit), reaching the model both through configure(maxsnow=) and through configure_otherargs so a continuation cannot revert it. The soil column is not exposed to unbounded snow either: landmod blends at most zsnowmax = 1 m of physical snow into it. Both facts are recorded at the code.

albsmaxf1/2 and albsminf1/2 are now a mixture of the band's exposed snow with the band's canopy albedo at a masked fraction, not a broadband ratio reapplied per band. landmod_nl gains albforest(2), forcovmx and forcovmn. The two fractions are solved from upstream's own Earth triple: 0.6153846*0.15 + 0.3846154*0.8 = 0.4 = albsmaxf and 0.4*0.15 + 0.6*0.4 = 0.3 = albsminf, so an Earth configuration reproduces upstream exactly, which is the check that can fail. run_exoplasim passes ALBFOREST = model.vegetation_albedo_bands = 0.075, 0.225 through configure_otherargs, so both the prepare and the resume path carry it. At full canopy the forested maxima move from 0.4914/0.2926 to 0.4241/0.3636 and the minima from 0.3685/0.2195 to 0.3347/0.2536: band 1 darker by 0.067, band 2 brighter by 0.071, +0.018 broadband. The two fractions differ from each other because upstream's two observational pairs do; that is recorded at the declaration rather than averaged away.

seamod's ramp is fractional and per band: zsicf = clamp((TMELT - dts)/dicealbdt, 0, 1), applied as dicealbmn(b) + zsicf*(dicealbmx(b) - dicealbmn(b)). Both bands now saturate at the same temperature, the anchor is TMELT rather than 273.0, and the formula returns exactly dicealbmn at the melting point instead of 0.004 below it. dicealbdt joins seamod_nl at 10.0 K, which is upstream's implied width at Earth's broadband span, so an Earth configuration keeps the same saturation temperature. albicemn replaces the literal 0.5 in the non-spectral copy, which is Earth's minimum sea-ice albedo. Measured against the staged endpoints: at 268 K band 2 goes 0.4645 -> 0.4083 and band 1 0.7608 -> 0.7679, -0.032 broadband; the largest broadband change over 263 to 273 K is -0.032 and the ends are within 0.004. Both call sites changed, seaini and seastep, and the calculation sits inside the where(dls < 0.5) block so it cannot read dts over land.

landstep and seastep now rebuild dalb from their own dsalb as zsolars(1)*dsalb(1,:) + zsolars(2)*dsalb(2,:) at nstartemp = 1, which is radmod.f90's own expression at the line that writes the diagnostic. Over land radmod's ocean direct-beam branch is gated on 1-dls, so dsalb is untouched there and code 175 now equals what the radiation used EXACTLY over snow, forested snow, glacier and the sea-ice fraction -- every surface the finding measured, where it read +0.057 to +0.068 high. One residual, named in the code and not left to be discovered: over the OPEN-WATER fraction radmod substitutes the ECHAM-3 zenith-angle direct-beam albedo when necham = 1 (the default, and this project does not override it), so 175 there is the flux-weighted doceanalb rather than the zenith-corrected value. Reproducing it would need radstep's local zmu0, which is not module state and is zonally averaged when ndcycle = 0. What replaced the Earth broadband albsea/albice pair is therefore a star-weighted ocean albedo rather than an exact one. Nothing the radiation reads changed: dsalb is untouched and at nstartemp = 0 both paths are unchanged. The six non-spectral scalars are left as they are rather than re-derived, because under two-band shortwave they now feed nothing but the nstartemp = 0 path. The 175 in/out collision is documented at surfmod.f90's surfcode rows -- staged background albedo per band in, dalb with the cryosphere blended into it out under pyburn's name alb/surface_albedo, and 176 not written out at all -- rather than renumbered, because staged .sra files and written output both depend on the numbering.

persistflag is replaced by persistt(NHOR), the seconds of continuous snow cover at or above GLACELIM, written to and read from the restart by glacierstop and glacierini. glacierstep resets it when cover breaks and converts the cell the moment it reaches glacpersec, so the conversion no longer waits for a segment boundary and no longer depends on where one falls. The duration is GLACPERSIST in glacier_nl, in ORBITS, converted by m_days_per_year * day_24hr -- the same conversion landini uses for tau_veg -- and declared in config/planet.yaml as surface.glaciers.persistence_orbits: 1.0, which is the duration a one-orbit-per-invocation caller was already enforcing, so the criterion is unchanged. It reaches both the prepare and the resume path through configure_otherargs. persistflag is DELETED rather than left set-and-never-read. NOT DONE HERE and filed as world-e1x: exoplasim/scripts/restart_schema.py needs a POLICY entry for persistt, and scripts/smoke_test.py's restart-schema check is red until it has one. That file belongs to another batch; the exact entry is in world-e1x.

zcvel and the pit-filling increment were parameter(4.2) and a literal 1.0 in two copies, landmod's roffini and glaciermod's oroini, of which oroini is the one that survives. Both now derive from landmod_nl keys: zcvel = roffvel*ga**(0.5-roffexp) and zoroinc = roffpit*ga. Because zoro is geopotential, that makes the velocity proportional to sqrt(ga) once the slope is divided back to a topographic one, which is the open-channel scaling; the exponent is written as (0.5-roffexp) so the two cannot drift apart. roffvel = 2.022845 reproduces 4.200 at ga = 9.80665, and roffpit = 0.101972 m reproduces 1.000 m2/s2, so an Earth configuration is unchanged -- an identity that can fail. At this planet's gravity the effective zcvel is 4.575, 1.0893x upstream's, which is the 1.14x from sqrt(g) less the 1.049x the geopotential slope was already supplying.

Both densities are DECLARED AS INHERITED with the bracket reported, which is the second arm of the acceptance criterion. rhosnow joins landmod_nl and rhoglac joins glacier_nl, values unchanged at 330 and 850 kg/m3, so the bracket can now be RUN rather than only stated. The declaration beside each says what the constant does -- rhosnow converts water equivalent to the physical snow thickness that insulates the soil column, rhoglac to the ice thickness that enters the orography -- and that both are settled densities set by overburden compaction, which scales with gravity, so both are low on a planet whose surface gravity is 1.306x the one they were measured on. Not rescaled: firn densification is not a closed-form function of gravity that can be evaluated here, and this project brackets an estimate it cannot verify rather than guessing it. The bracket is the issue's own, roughly 10 to 20 per cent on snow insulation thickness and on glacier relief. glaciermod already had the GRAVITY right in the orography conversion, with its own comment; the density beside it is the half that is inherited, and that is now said where the two meet.

SIMBA stays OFF -- nothing enables it and nveg is untouched. Both traps are disarmed rather than recorded. Trap 1: vegini now REFUSES nveg = 2 with nstartemp = 1 and stops, because vegstep sets dalb and not dsalb, so under a two-band shortwave SIMBA's vegetation albedo would reach the radiation nowhere while its roughness and its soil water bucket reached it everywhere. The positive form is a per-band vegetation albedo and there is no derivation for one, so the refusal is the decision procedure until there is. Trap 2: 'dwmax(jhor) = zwmax' is gated on NVEGWMAX, a new vegmod_nl key, and vegini states at initialisation which field owns the soil water bucket. The default is 1 -- SIMBA, upstream's behaviour, preserved exactly -- so nothing changes for anyone running it today, but a run can now keep the pedology-derived staged code-229 field instead of having it silently overwritten every timestep. The module header carries both items and, separately, the Earth calibrations that are approximate rather than broken: rlue against dfd(:,NLEP), the BROADBAND downward shortwave, rather than the photosynthetically active fraction; ct_crit's linear ramp from TMELT with no optimum and no high-temperature cutoff; q10's 283.16 K reference; Harvey's beta factor; the biome fits; and vsalb_min as a THIRD independent forested-snow albedo constant, now inconsistent with landmod's albforest masking as well as with the spectrum. Deletion was considered as the alternative and not taken: surfmod, plasimmod, the restart records and the output code table all reference the module, so removing it is a cross-batch change rather than a fix.

The two endmembers are re-weighted by the same derivation the third went through and moved to the same place. analysis/vegetation_albedo.py gains COVER_ENDMEMBERS and writes cover_albedo, cover_albedo_earth_sun and cover_albedo_bracket; config/planet.yaml gains model.tree_albedo 0.143 (from 0.13) and model.grass_albedo 0.209 (from 0.19) with brackets [0.130, 0.148] and [0.190, 0.217]; and build_surface_albedo.py's two flags default to the config with no silent Earth-Sun fallback, which is the rule --vegetation-albedo already followed. The POPULATION leaf ratio 1.1002 rather than the per-class one: tree and grass differ by 0.006 in ratio and 0.001 in albedo, and the grass class has four spectra in it, so a per-class ratio would not resolve the effect it claims to separate. lib/provenance.py: the two keys and their brackets join the inert sets of the three builders that never read them, and are deliberately absent from surface_albedo's, which does; check_consistency's re-grep confirms both halves. Discovered and filed as world-36g rather than fixed here: --mode modelled still writes ONE identical field to codes 174, 175 and 176, because the band split SPEC-5 added is gated on --mode vegetated, and splitting the modelled blend needs a band pair for the rock table that does not exist.

Fixed in 1b9aa183. Both literals are rainmod_nl keys. clwhsc, the e-folding length coefficient, DERIVES from the model's own gascon and ga (700*(gascon/ga)/(287.0/9.80665), returning 700 at Earth's values) because it is a length and the heights it is measured against are already built that way; a positive namelist value overrides. clwref, the reference in-cloud liquid density, is exposed UNCHANGED at Kiehl's value: it is a condensate concentration with no gravity dependence, so no consistency argument moves it, and its bracket is world-8h6. This CHANGES RESULTS -- thinner high cloud, slightly thicker low cloud, simulated mean down on both the longwave trap and the shortwave reflection -- and is recorded as an unpriced row in forcing-bundle-predictions.md, because pricing needs a baseline climatology and config declares none. Needs a rebuild (rule 4).

Both rung lints now scan *.sh, the path lint recognises .x, and check_no_rung_table_outside_rungs is new: it catches a rung literal beside its own dimensions (twice in a file) and a line carrying three or more of the ladder's bare latitude counts. Fixed by routing through lib/rungs.py: verify_transform_roundtrip.sh, verify_gauss_weights.sh, filter_timestep_matrix.py; make_profile_bed.py's help string no longer names a rung. Exempted by name with reasons: verify_fold_indexing.sh and verify_fold_exactness.sh (unrunnable, paths point at a gone worktree -- world-en0), restart_convert_selftest.py (source-target grid pairs, no rung names). RUNG_OWNER became a mapping so every exemption states its reason. cache_budget.py's table is the one remaining hit and is NOT exempted: world-qjq already removed it in another fan-out worktree, so the lint goes green on merge.

hdiffo took the planet radius from planet_nl by way of pumamod; oceanmod's parameter(PLARAD=6.371E6) is gone, oceanini aborts if nhdiff>0 with no radius and logs the radius it will use. LABEL vs VALUE: hdiffk's meaning is unchanged and its effect changes. An arm declaring 1000 m2/s now diffuses at 1000 m2/s where it diffused at (a_earth/a)**2 * 1000. So clim-16's measured 300/1000/3000 bracket was really 432/1440/4320 and its diffusivity labels are wrong by 1.44x; its conservation claim does not depend on the coefficient's value and is untouched. clim-65 must declare its arms in true units. Dormant in every run to date, NHDIFF=0 everywhere. Commit 893dbb1e.

cpl_stub.f90 rewritten: clsgini, clsgstep and clsgstop now declare exactly what cpl.f90 declares and what oceanmod.f90 and plasim_dummy.f90 pass, and each calls mpabort. A build linked against the stub has no LSG in it, so NLSG>0 on it is a configuration that cannot be honoured; the previous no-op also returned pfldo untouched, which oceanstep then scattered from an uninitialised local. Unchanged wherever NLSG=0, which is every run. Verified by grep over the whole tree: the only other call sites are plasim_dummy.f90 (not compiled), and they match too. Commit cb78c7cf.

CRHOS, CPS and CLFI are icemod_nl keys; icemod passes all four salinity constants into oceanini so the two modules cannot hold different sea water, and oceanmod's own parameter copies are gone. CONSUMERS ENUMERATED: CPS reaches (a) the mixed-layer heat capacity CRHOS*CPS in mksst, mkiflux, addfc, mkfc and the entropy diagnostics, and through mkiflux's residual flux it reaches ice growth as well as the SST tendency; icemod's own CPS was declared and never used, and is now the source of truth it passes down. CRHOS additionally is the snow-ice flooding threshold in subsnow as CRHOS-CRHOI. CLFI appears only as CRHOI*CLFI, latent heat per m3 of ice, in icestep, mkice, mkflukoi, addfci and oceanmod's addfc. CRHOF is declared in icemod and used nowhere. VALUES: CPS's compiled default corrected from 4180 (fresh water at about 25 C) to 3990.34 (sea water at S=34.7 and its freezing point); CRHOS and CLFI keep their compiled defaults and are only exposed. run_exoplasim derives CRHOS and CPS from config's salinity by EOS-80 and the UNESCO (1983) polynomial, each checked against published check values and against the constant CPS replaces; CLFI is declared in config because it depends on the ice's own salinity and temperature and the model has no such variable. All four go through configure_otherargs, so they survive a continuation, and through expected_namelist_keys. At the declared salinity the run configuration moves to CRHOS 1027.94 and CPS 3990.33: mixed-layer heat capacity down 5.1 per cent, so a declared 50 m mixed layer is 50 m of sea water rather than 52.5, and the flooding margin CRHOS-CRHOI from 110 to 107.94. Every run and climatology on disk is superseded (rule 7). Commit 9c952a18.

A cold start with no codes 169/210/211 now begins from a DECLARED profile or refuses to begin. read_ice_surface no longer constructs ice cover from the SST sentinel; make_ice_thickness's CCM3 relation is reachable only when a real cover was read, and warns that it is Earth-fitted and hemispherically asymmetric. ice_cold_start takes either the read climatology or icemod_nl's tsst_eq/tsst_pol/hice_ini profile, tsst_pol + (tsst_eq-tsst_pol)*cos(lat)**2, symmetric by construction, and aborts if neither exists. oceanmod's yclsst gains its -999 initialiser (module-scope SAVE, which -finit-real does not reach) and the ocean starts from the declared profile rather than from memory clipped to freezing. xicecc is set from the initial cover on BOTH paths, which is the fix for sic being identically zero beside a non-zero sit: mkicec only grows it and icestep copies it into xicec every step. config/planet.yaml declares ocean.cold_start and run_exoplasim writes TSST_EQ/TSST_POL/HICE_INI on a prepare and on every resume; expected_namelist_keys checks them. The declared cold start is ice-free, which is the side of the hysteresis the flux sweep could not reach; an arm that wants the iced side declares a sub-freezing pole or a non-zero thickness. WHAT DEPENDED ON THE OLD BEHAVIOUR: all 9 runs in exoplasim/runs cold-started from the constructed field and the ocean at freezing, and every restart carries it forward; per rule 7 the canonical climatology lineage does not exist, so all of it is disposable. NO RESTART RECORD ADDED OR CHANGED. Commit b5918b94.

nfluko cannot relax toward a constructed field: it is refused outright when there is no read climatology, on the -999 sentinel in xclsst/yclsst, which is a restart record so a continuation that switches nfluko on is refused the same way a cold start is. nfluko=1's two correction fields, codes 709 and 903, get sentinels of their own so 'absent' is not read as 'zero everywhere'. The same refusal covers the three other branches that prescribe rather than integrate a surface: nice=0, ntskin=0 and oceanmod's nocean=0. VERIFIED, not assumed: every consumer of the constructed field enumerated by grep over icemod.f90 and oceanmod.f90. Guarded by the abort - icestep's nice==0 block, its nfluko==1 block (xicec from xclicec2, and the xmaxd clause), mkflukoi, addfci, oceanmod's addfc, mkfc, getflxco and the nocean==0 block. Clamped harmless - iceget's AMAX1 makes xclicec2/xcliced2 zero, which is what iceout codes 790/791 and oceanstep's pcliced argument then see; xflxice2 and yfsst2 are set to zero on the nfluko==0 branch. Diagnostic only - the nprint==2 blocks, and ocean output code 990 which emits the sentinel and is in no pyburn code table and read by no script here. Dead - mkicecf is never called. Nothing else reads them. scripts/error_budget.py's no-q-flux item now records that a q-flux is not available on this world at any price. analysis/error_budget.json is absent from this tree and needs a baseline climatology, so it picks the text up on its next run. Commits b5918b94, 3a368340.

zh0 is now icemod_nl's HLEAD, declared in config at ExoPlaSim's value: exposed, not changed, and it reproduces the compiled 0.5 exactly. It was a local in both mkicec (live) and mkicecf (dead) and both now read the module value. getiflx is DELETED. The thickness limit's melt is paid out of the same cell's conductive flux to the ocean instead of a global area-weighted sum spread over every other cell with ice below the limit; the old form was a heat transport with no carrier and it also dropped the remainder silently whenever demand exceeded capacity, since xcfluxr is reset at the top of every icestep. xmaxd is DECLARED OFF (-1.0) in config/planet.yaml and written to the namelist, so the branch cannot fire in any arm. The argument: 9 m is Earth's Arctic multi-year maximum standing in for ice export, which this model does not have and which the error budget already carries as a declared structural term; and xmaxd is not only a clamp, because mkcflux and skintemp zero the conductive flux once ice reaches it, so a positive value stops basal growth outright. Conductive growth goes as the square root of time, so switching it off leaves nothing unbounded. Dormant at the current climate, so the baseline is unchanged. XMAXD and HLEAD are both in configure_otherargs and expected_namelist_keys. Commit 9e6372e1.

albedo_mode now takes the endmember from source_config.model.land_albedo_source on the run's own manifest, with no fallback; the land-mean albedo is still measured from the run's staged SRA and reported beside it. Instrument-versus-effect: the endmembers' separation survived (0.0824 against the 0.092 the 0.256 cut was placed in) but both moved BELOW the cut -- 0.2483 bare rock, 0.1659 vegetated -- so the classifier kept its resolution and lost its placement, which is why the fix is not a better cut point. Added a check that fails when two arms at one flux were handed the same land-mean albedo. Verified: the old rule returns 'vegetated' for both of today's endmembers; the new one returns 'lithology' for a lithology manifest and raises where the declaration is absent. Every run on disk declares vegetated, so 'cannot bracket' is now a true statement about the run set.

Fixed in a5c469f0. ozone_height_m and ozone_spread_m are declared in config/planet.yaml at upstream's 20000 and 5000 scaled by (gascon/ga) over Earth's own (0.765592 at gascon 287.017 from the declared composition, ga 12.81), and configure_otherargs writes BO3 and CO3 from them on prepare and on every resume, checked by verify_staged_namelists. Top-layer column share reported in exoplasim/notes/ozone.md, measured by reproducing mko3's recursion on the model's own ten sigma levels: 0.4184 at Earth gravity, 0.6718 here at 20 km, and the pressure-equivalent placement returns every layer to the Earth-gravity value to machine precision. No Fortran change was needed.

Correction to the issue: __init__.py did NOT need a line. Earthlike.configure forwards **kwargs, and configure(), loadconfig() and exportcfg() all handle the ozone dict already. The driver was routed away from that dict deliberately -- it also rewrites A0O3, A1O3, ACO3 and TOFFO3, which would turn four more Earth constants into transcriptions in run_exoplasim.py, and those four are the separate profile-SHAPE question the ozone note records.
Applied on the coordination branch: persistt entered in restart_schema.POLICY as PROGNOSTIC_GRID/REMAP/INTENSIVE, domain land, bounds (0.0, None). smoke_test 22/22.

model.lake_dwmax_m declared in config/planet.yaml and the builder's .get(..., 0.2) fallback removed: it now refuses without the key. Value preserved at 0.2 m, so no staged field changes. The direction IS derived (drhs reaches 1 above 40% of dwmax, landmod.f90:52-53, so a shallower bucket saturates the wetness factor on less water, and the lakes sit in arid cells); the value is not, and world-kvr is that derivation, blocked on a baseline climatology. lib/provenance.py marks the key inert for surface_albedo, surface_roughness and boundary_conditions, traced by the same grep the other entries use; live for surface_soil_water, whose provenance record now correctly reads stale against config. Deliberately NOT added to continue_exoplasim's resume allowlist, because it changes a staged field; no run is spinup_in_progress, so nothing in flight is blocked.

Applied on the coordination branch. Batch B's half (radstop's comment recording why the write is kept and that nothing reads it back) merged with the batch; the schema row is now OPAQUE/TARGET per B's decision, so a converter no longer refuses over a value radstart recomputes. smoke_test 22/22.

Applied on the coordination branch to batch F's spec. Code 151 dropped from REGULAR_CODES and SNAPSHOT_CODES (this project's lists, not a vendored default); RLAPSE -> RLAPSE_EARTH and the bare 255.0 -> PSL_COLD_GUARD_K_EARTH in pyburn.py, both documented as Earth defaults reachable only by an explicit request for 151. alv, als and tmelt are in planet_nl on p_earth.f90, the module that compiles, at the values plasimmod.f90 already declared, and plasim.f90 broadcasts all three because they are threadprivate and only NROOT reads the namelist. The PLASIM_PLANET axis is removed from CMakeLists.txt and p_earth.f90 is a literal source: it admitted only a module that could not compile as its alternative, build_model.py never set it, and this build has one planet. p_mars.f90 and p_exo.f90 are deleted under world-cmz. Commit 3098acef.

Thirteen of the sixteen uncompiled sources deleted, list re-derived from CMakeLists.txt as it stands: cpl.f90, guimod.f90, icemod_template.f90, outdiag.f90, p_exo.f90, p_mars.f90, plasim_dummy.f90, pumax.c, rainmod_bm.f90, rainmod_kuo_old.f90, rainmod_mca.f90, readdat.f90, resmod_def.f90. newsnow.f90 and buildice.f90 kept for clim-53; mpimod_multi.f90 left to world-38b. Rule 4: all five binaries need rebuild_binaries.py and --verify; no compiled line moved. Commit 2332dd76.

Deleted under world-cmz, commit 2332dd76. It was in no _sources list and in no variant slot, and the five divergences from icemod.f90 were the argument for removing it rather than for levelling a file that compiles nowhere.

Deleted: hpc/ (11 files), pRT.py, colormatch.py, randomcontinents.py, quickprocess.py, plus Model.transit, Model.image and the pRTopts option surface that existed only for pRT. surfacespecs.py is NOT dead and the issue's premise on it was wrong: analysis/ice_albedo.py, the ice_albedo step in config/pipeline.yaml, loads it by file path and reads its eight named reflectance arrays. What was fixed instead is the unconditional import in __init__.py, so importing the package no longer globs and loads every basespecs/*.npy. basespecs/ retained as the ECOSTRESS component spectra any re-blend of this world's surface albedos would start from. Commit 08ce9ce7.

[projection.optional-dependencies] renamed to [project.optional-dependencies], so the extras resolve. pRT dropped with the module it served; basemap dropped because its only appearance is in commented-out code in gcmt.py. h5, nc and mpl all still have live readers. Verified by tomllib parse.

make_most, most.c, setup.py and MANIFEST.in deleted; sysconfigure(), printsysconfig() and the firstrun block in Model.__init__ removed. The firstrun block was not merely dormant: on a fresh clone it set recompile=True and the recompile branch REFUSES rather than builds, so the first Model constructed would have aborted with SystemExit even with its executable present. config/planet.yaml's most_compiler_mpi claim and the fork .gitignore's configure.sh/compile.sh framing both now describe the CMake build; docs/src/reference/vendored-upstreams.md names all of it in the fork's deletion list. Commit e9870295. NOT done and separate: vendor/exoplasim/docs/index.rst still documents upstream's configure/compile install path and references sysconfigure and printsysconfig - filed separately.

vendor/exoplasim falls 171 MB -> 47 MB. Deleted lsg/, puma/, sam/, cat/, cat_tools/, octave/, images/, exoplasim_testers/, glacier/, postprocessor/ + plasim/run/burn7.x, plasim/dat/, the CAT manuals, Plasim_Report/, the configure-era compiler probes and the sibling-model scripts, plus four stray probe run logs at exoplasim/exoplasim/bench/. plasim/bld/ was already gone. burn7.x no longer reaches a run directory and its .gitignore re-include is removed. KEPT against the list, each with a named reader: basespecs/ (analysis/ice_albedo.py via surfacespecs), hazeconstants/ (Model.configure stages an aerofile from it), tools/ (the restart-converter note names pusca.f90's convert_restart_array as its base). Manuals decided and recorded in docs/src/reference/vendored-upstreams.md: PlaSim RM, PlaSim UG and PUMA UG stay; the CAT manuals and the climate report go. Commit 1bbdf63c.

About 1,400 lines removed, list re-derived by a comment-stripped token sweep of every .f90 and .c in plasim/src plus the repository outside it, excluding vendor/cgenie (which ships its own PlaSim, so every name appears there) and excluding prose. INTERFACE blocks counted as references and caught ndayofyear, which radmod.f90 declared twice while both call sites were commented out. Removed: check_equality, cosa, cosc, fyppm, dtodat, ndayofyear, surfname, orb_print, n2mmr, writecolumn, sp3fc, shtns_teardown, planet_stop, guistep_puma, guihorlsg, mkicecf + CRHOF, earthveg (322 lines), and in the omp layer mrsum, mrbci, mpgallgp, mpgathersp, mpreadgp, mpreadsp, mpwritegp, mpwritesp, mpgadn and the four finish variants (from all three utilities files). From pyburn: readvariablecode, _getknownwordlength, _getmarkerlength, f2py_compile and _gettimevar. KEPT with reader named: mpsumr (verify_omp_collectives.f90 calls it - the issue was wrong), mpwritegph (37 call sites), nweekday (tools/caltest.f90). The mpimod.f90/mpimod_multi.f90/mpimod_stub.f90 copies of the dead collectives left to world-38b, which deletes those files whole. Rule 4: all five binaries need rebuild and --verify. Commit fad2a2fa.

Both removed under world-ro6, commit fad2a2fa. mkicecf and the CRHOF parameter each had exactly one occurrence in the tree - their own declaration - checked against every .f90 and .c in plasim/src with comments stripped and against the repository outside it, with vendor/cgenie's own PlaSim copy excluded.

continue_exoplasim.py passes filterkappa and filterpower and calls declare_hyperdiffusion; expected_namelist_keys covers FILTERKAPPA, NFILTEREXP, NHDIFF, NDEL and the four TDISS* arrays, the last five compared as replicated text so a scalar cannot pass. No numeric changed.

The four global means in gridpointa are area-weighted, summed locally and reduced, which also drops four full-globe gathers per diagnostic step. Two helpers in plasim.f90 do the weighting in one place: gpareamean for a distributed field, ugpmean for a gathered one. ncountsea's land and sea percentages and the fifteen 'Mean:' orography and icesheet prints in glaciermod and surfmod follow. NO PUBLISHED NUMBER MOVES: the only reader of t2mean, precip, evap and olr is energy(), which passes them to guiput, and CMakeLists compiles guimod_stub.f90 whose guiput is a bodyless return.

nflux, npackgp, npacksp, nsurf, zeta and ngpitrigger are gone from their groups, declarations, broadcasts and the shipped templates. nguidbg and sellon leave plasim_nl and the template but keep their module declarations, because their only reader is the uncompiled guimod.f90 and the compiled build passes sellon to bodyless column routines. nguidbg's second declaration in carbonmod's private plasim_nl had to go with it: that group WRITES a namelist plasim_nl no longer declares the name in.

nfixer removed rather than wired up: negative specific humidity is not a state the model may integrate, so 'off' was never a configuration. The fixer's mass redistribution is recorded at the routine -- it conserves the column integral except where the global deficit exceeds the global surplus, where it is a sink -- and close_state_energy.py names it against its vapour reservoir.

oroscale enters planet_nl in all three planet modules and the API writes OROSCALE to planet_namelist. planet_nl is the only group that can hold it: every reader runs inside surface_ini and planet_ini is the only namelist read before that. NDESERT now goes to plasim_namelist on both branches; the desertplanet=False arm wrote landmod_namelist, which does not declare it, so turning it off aborted the run.

hcadencesc and hcadencediag deleted with the commented-out call that was hcadencediag's only call site. The absence of a scalar record is the decision and is stated at the high-cadence output block: the stream exists for DUST-5's gust distribution, HIGH_CADENCE_CODES is the winds, its time axis comes from the code 139 record hcadencegp already writes, and one orbit is 15 GB before anything is added.

model.vertical_grid and model.model_top_hpa declare NEQSIG 4 and PTOP 5000 Pa, both scripts pass them, expected_namelist_keys covers them. Values unchanged. parameter-decisions.md corrected: modeltop was NOT None -- at None, configure's truthiness test fails, PTOP is never written and the model uses plasimmod's compiled 7500 Pa; 5000 came from Earthlike's own 50 hPa pin. The quartic's coefficients are derived where they are written.

mkdheat's two sp2fl calls inside if(nenergy > 0) now take sh_sp2gp into hddt_g under nshtns == 1, with the wrapper's barriers, and the 'off by default' comment is gone. Filed world-3ya for the thirteen more live per-timestep legmod transforms in spectrala and spectrald that CLIM-64 also missed; they need shared _g destinations first, which is why mkdheat could move and they could not.

calini takes m_days_per_year, m_days_per_month and mtspd from the caller, so the calendar day is the 24-hour day and tcalday comes out at day_24hr by construction. readnl gains a setter for m_days_per_month, the year over twelve rounded up. cal2step uses m_days_* and kyea-1, making it the exact inverse of step2cal30 over three years of steps and making year 1 month 1 day 1 encode to step 0 -- which also moves every cold start's orbital phase from 0.799 to 0. Residual drift 0.10 per cent against 1.54. calini aborts on n_days_per_year == 365 with the reason.

ra1i/ra2i/ra4i added to pumamod and planet_nl in all three planet modules at 610.66/21.875/7.65; three elemental selectors ra1s/ra2s/ra4s branch per gridpoint. Thirty-two sites in rainmod, two in landmod and one in simba take the temperature in the expression. fluxmod's two take the phase from the where arm and seamod's two stay liquid, because fluxmod treats every cell with dls < 0.5 as evaporating liquid whatever its temperature. This is a physics change and moves the climate.

The NTRU==42 .and. NLEV==10 gamma override is removed rather than re-keyed: gamma is a fraction of the deficit per TIMESTEP, both rungs run the same step, and a 43 per cent jump on a rung change makes every cross-rung comparison carry a precipitation-physics change. Every run is T21 and integrated 0.01, unchanged. resolution-tuned-parameters.md corrected: the T42 branch was never hit.

Each of fluxmod's constants carries a statement of what it is and that the ECHAM value is kept because nothing here has measured a replacement. ztscal joins fluxmod_nl at the same 250 K. zumin is squared at the mktcoe site so it means m/s at both of its uses; at the declared 1 m/s nothing moves. THE FREE-CONVECTION COEFFICIENT MOVES THE SURFACE FLUXES: 0.0016 is Miller's with Earth's g folded in and w* goes as g^(1/3), so it was low by 1.093 and free-convection exchange over calm unstable ocean was about 9 per cent weak. fluxini derives it from ga.

enable_dust_emission reads the AEROFILE's own provenance sidecar beside the .dat it already stages and writes APART and RHOP from it, refusing if the sidecar is missing or either value is not positive. Two provenance files reach that function and the distinction is load-bearing: the source-field sidecar carries the emission law, the aerofile sidecar carries the grain. in-model-dust.md corrected -- it asserted the sidecar was already the run's source of radius, and no code path opened it.

Declared as anchored to T21 rather than re-keyed, because a per-rung table would be the same undeclared fit written more times. snowcovz is now one named key in landmod_nl at 0.01, replacing a bare literal at six sites in landmod and one in simba. rcrit's 0.85 floor, the zcca/zccb cloud-cover fit, glaciermod's 30 m flag on a cell-mean depth and hurricanemod's four grid-unit thresholds carry the statement in place. dls > 0.5 has no rung-independent form and is recorded as such. resolution-tuned-parameters.md section 4 is the list SPAT-8 attributes its cross-rung differences to. No numeric changed.

VERDICT: DELETED, 447 lines across ten modules. 'Enabled and consumed' was not available -- the blocks write codes 320-355 and 420-442, and 320/321 are already tempmin/tempmax on the same stream, in REGULAR_CODES, mapped by pyburn as mint/maxt, while 322-329 collide with the hurricane diagnostics; pyburn has no entry for any entropy code. Enabling them needed a renumbering nobody had asked for, so the switch was a trap. FORMULATION CHECK, against the code not the documentation. The finding is now a measurement rather than a level count. The baseline climatology's bottom two sigma levels are 0.98282 and 0.92191; through the hypsometric relation at this world's gravity and a 280 K near-surface temperature that is a lowest full level near 110 m and a second near 510 m, so two levels below a kilometre and one below half. A Bodele-class nocturnal inversion and the jet core above it both fall inside the single lowest layer, whose wind is that layer's mean. The obstacle is not that the jet is weakly resolved, it is that the model has no interior to the layer the jet lives in, so no amount of high-cadence sampling recovers it.

Gravity neither causes nor relieves it: sigma levels sit at heights proportional to the scale height and the nocturnal boundary layer compresses by the same factor, so the count of levels inside it is unchanged. 1.31 g concentrates the same surface cooling into less air, which makes the regime more likely to matter, not more likely to resolve.

The instruction file's values corroborate the declarations, 0.33 for both steps of the reduction sequence against 0.1 and the nitrification gas share. Four declarations against one use, so the reads moved and nothing was renamed; the NO2-to-gas ceiling is now 0.33 where it was 0.25, a factor of 1.32 on that coefficient. Both rate ceilings stay unsourced and refusing: table 9 eqns 3 and 4 carry no maximum-rate constant and table 11 lists none, and no value was invented for either.

The min(1, .) is gone from f_den_T; the response is now exactly Xu-Ri and Prentice (2008) table 9 eqn 1, which carries none. It is 1.21 at 25 C, 1.61 at 30 C, 2.07 at 35 C, 3.15 at 45 C and 8.07 at the top of the declared temperature domain, so warm-soil denitrification is no longer held at its 22 C rate. The premise that something had to bound it was wrong: both transformations it multiplies are already written as min(pool, pool * coefficient), so neither can take more nitrogen out of a pool than the pool holds. That is now declared as clamped_by on the two denitrification products, and the gate checks the min() is still in the source rather than requiring a product below 1. The -40 C guard stays: the exponent diverges at -46.02 C and the function is 5e-21 there.

nh3_max is removed. The operator's ammonia multiplier is now exactly Xu-Ri and Prentice (2008) table 5 eqns 2, 3, 4 and 6, whose fpH = exp(2*(pH-10)) already carries the NH3/NH4 ratio the paper's text describes. It was a rate constant nowhere in the paper and a duplicate of fpH, plus a factor-100 step at pH 6 on a smooth exponential. Over pedology's pH range the daily coefficient of NH4_mass now reaches 9.2e-2 where it reached 9.2e-5: at pH 6.5 it is at most 2.3e-4 per day against 2.3e-7, and at pH 8.5 1.2e-2 against 1.2e-5. Calibration entry function:nh3_multiplier is now 'agrees'.

Both matric heads in get_mineral are clamped at Psi_s, the air-entry value, so Theta_whc and Theta_wilt cannot exceed Theta_s. Cosby et al. (1984) eqn 1 holds only below air entry; above it the pore space is full. The code is what keeps it right now, not the map. No cell of either current Vesper soil map is in the affected corner (sand at or below about 0.10 with clay at or below about 0.26), both maps being sand 0.17 or above, so no current soil property changes. Declared, not fitted. substrate_partition keeps richards_curve(0.05, 0.95, 7.5, 0.5, wfps) and the refusal is narrowed into two entries because the midpoint and the shape are unsettled to different degrees: function:wet_fraction carries the midpoint 0.5 with its 0.50-0.66 bracket, the spread between Pilegaard's 0.60 crossover and the operator's own comment's 66 per cent, with the declared value at the bottom edge; form:wet_fraction_shape carries the shape parameter 7.5, which has no source and no bracket at all. Xu-Ri and Prentice (2008) settles the argument and only the argument, delegating the form to PnET-DNDC's anaerobic balloon. No number was moved: a midpoint picked from a bracket neither paper states would be an invention dressed as a source.

Re-derived, but against Xu-Ri rather than Weier, which is the third option the Do line did not list and is better than either it did. The partition is now table 9 eqns 5, 6 and 7 with table 11's RNODN (under 0.2 per cent) and RN2ODN (0.2-4.7 per cent, stated mean 2 per cent), so NO and N2O are RNODN*ftemp and RN2ODN*ftemp of the reduced NO2 and N2 is the remainder, at every water-filled pore space. That removes the branch at 0.7 WFPS, the hard zero N2 below it that Weier tables 4 and 5 refute directly, the N2O:NO regression attributed to a paper that never measured NO, the N2O:N2 curve and the logistic in temperature from a single-temperature study: four unsourced calibration entries collapse into one that agrees with its source. What it does not settle is the size of the N2 share, 0.978 at 22 C against Weier's medians 0.565, 0.744 and 0.796, union interquartile 0.333-0.938. Two Earth calibrations disagree; the operator runs at the DyN end because every other equation in it is DyN's, and form:denitrification_n2_share carries that disagreement as an 'outside' verdict owned by world-bzqj. Total denitrification does not move and all three gases leave the soil, so the partition changes what is reported and not what the simulated plants can reach. Also registered while rewriting the function: the 0.4 WFPS threshold below which the operator denitrifies nothing, which neither paper states, as world-q4qy.

THE TABULATION BIAS IS BOUNDED AND HAS THE WRONG SIGN. The within-class spread is measured, not asserted: Prigent et al. (2005) Table 1 carries three groups of repeat in-situ values for the same area, and pooling their within-box variance of ln z0 gives a geometric standard deviation of 2.736 with eleven degrees of freedom, bracketed 1.297 to 5.095 by the single-box extremes. It is an upper bound on the within-lithology spread because a Death Valley box holds several surface types. Declared in dust.yaml under drag_partition.within_class_z0 as a REPORTED bias rather than folded into the arms, because each class's bracket is the same kind of range and evaporite's is explicitly MacKinnon's spread over one measurement set; using it twice would double count.

THE CORRECTION IS ONE-SIGNED, so the reported intensity is a floor on that axis and the reopening crossing in notes/dust.md is a floor too. THE TEXTURE SENSITIVITY IS RUN AND TEXTURE IS NOT THE LEVER HERE, for a structural reason. This world's erodible substrate is clay-rich closed-basin fill and evaporite crust, so 86.9 percent of the emission and 91.6 percent of the erodible area sit at or above Kok's declared f_clay cap, where texture cannot move the flux through that term at all. Under this project's own Earth-calibrated clay (pedology/analysis/earth_validation.json, slope 1.1096, intercept -0.0382) the emission moves 5.7 percent; across the validation RMSE it spans 0.608 to 1.326; halving and doubling the clay spans 4.2. All far below the roughness bracket's 10.6. So the roughness bracket is not carrying uncertainty that belongs to the texture.

THE GEOMETRY ROUTE THIS ISSUE PROPOSED WAS TESTED AND DOES NOT WORK, and that is recorded so it is not tried again. Erodible connected components on the 10M-region export are basin-fill provinces whose area-weighted 99th percentile is 4.3e6 km2, not playas; the area-weighted median height above a component's own floor is 81 m and only 15 percent of erodible area lies within 10 m of it. snowmaskmod is the operator: masked fraction from canopy cover, canopy exposure above the snow surface (uniform vertical plant area, 1 - z_snow/h_canopy in metres of snow), gap fraction of the plant area (1 - exp(-k L)), and the fraction of the canopy holding snow, which brightens the masking canopy toward the exposed-snow endmember rather than being masked -- so ground snow and canopy snow are separate states. Form from Essery (2013)'s gap-fraction scheme, which is also the cited reason a two-stream canopy is a bracket rather than an improvement and is not built; no Earth forest albedo is imported, every albedo is the caller's under this star. The dforest blend is preserved BITWISE at the shipped values, and exoplasim/scripts/verify_snow_mask.sh is the check: the reduction over a cover/depth sweep, the four named limits with answers written in advance, bounds and both monotonicities, and it fails on a one-ulp mutation of the operator. The gap-fraction comparison is reported: upstream's two masking fractions read back through the same law are plant area indices of about 0.96 and 0.51 at an extinction coefficient of one, so the scalar mask is weak in gap-fraction terms. Every structural axis is inert and they are scalars standing in for fields; driving them from reported canopy height and plant area, which needs accepted vegetation (bio-17) and explicit permission, is bio-33, and the prognostic canopy snow store that would predict interception and unloading is bio-32. Verified by building the T21 l10 p16 production configuration in the worktree and by verify_model_compiles.py.

Delivered as hydrography/config/land_water_ledger.yaml, hydrography/scripts/land_water_ledger.py and hydrography/notes/land-water-ledger.md, with a pipeline row and surface_water and groundwater needing it. Ten control volumes from the air column over a land cell to a terminal boundary at the coast; twenty-one directed terms in kilograms of water, each with one source, one destination, one owner, a declared interval floor and the artifact that would supply it; seven named absences; and one owner per store with every shadow copy in a second component written down. Two invariants: water held in reservoirs plus water at terminal nodes equals water held at the start plus water across boundary nodes, and each evaporative component is debited by exactly one term from exactly one store -- the second is checked separately because the mass identity does not imply it. Eleven closure fixtures, ten built wrong in a named way and required to be rejected, including the shadow store that credits the atmosphere a flux the domain was never debited and the positive P-E spent as bucket overflow, catchment runoff and recharge at once. Twelve mutations of the declaration that the graph check must catch, so the check is falsifiable. Every term carries the undeclared sentinel by design: the ledger is what LSHY-1, LSHY-3, LSHY-4, LSHY-5 and PLHY-4 deliver INTO, and --strict refuses while any term is undeclared, any store has a shadow copy, or any producer supplies only an annual mean to a store that changes inside the year. lib/gridding.py now carries the field-specific operators, applied at two call sites and documented in CLAUDE.md's lib list: cell_sum for extensive stores and fluxes (global total preserved exactly), cell_mean for intensives over an explicit population, cell_fraction for categorical retained fractions, cell_moments for the statistic a cell-scale parameter may consume (two-pass variance about the cell mean, because the difference-of-moments form every consumer had written returns round-off on a constant field), cell_expectation for the process-then-aggregate order (takes the law as a callable so the order cannot be got wrong at the call site), and transfer_ledger for what a reduction dropped. python lib/gridding.py --selftest asserts ten invariants on synthetic input with no build on disk: extensive closure, constant preservation, population closure, categorical partition, zero variance on a constant field against a bar that the form this replaced misses by nine orders, moments against a direct per-cell computation, a linear law's expectation equalling the law of the mean, a CONVEX NEGATIVE CONTROL that must show a strictly positive gap, ledger closure, and periodicity of the column expression.

hydrography/scripts/build_groundwater_access.py reduces water_table.nc onto the climate grid as an AREA and never as a mean depth. The access criterion is evaluated on the NATIVE REGIONS, where the depth lives, and what crosses is the fraction of the cell's land below each declared access depth, with the extensive area beside it. No hypsometry is used and none is needed: the within-cell depth distribution is in hand, so reconstructing it from GRID-2's would be an inference where there is a measurement -- that hypsometry is for criteria that are terrain-conditioned and have no native evaluation.

sink_fraction crosses as three regime area shares plus its own undefined share, at_surface and the excluded lithologies as their own shares, and the Gleeson permeability bracket as a member axis (--water-table once per member, labelled by each file's sigma). So the regime flags hydrography/README.md requires every depth consumer to preserve are preserved by construction rather than by discipline.

Every fraction is a fraction of the cell's own LAND population from surface_class, so there is no per-region access fraction: GW-6, and world-d9u4's constraint, the same one topographic_index states for f_sat_max.

The step guards its own index alignment with gridding.require_index_alignment against the coupling matrix for the same rung.

THE VERDICT. The gate does not transport, and it is NOT the compound topographic index's failure mode. CTI shifts by exactly ln 2 because its argument a/tan(beta) carries a LENGTH, so the shift is deterministic and subtractable. A gradient is a length over a length and carries none; it fails because the surface is self-affine, so the shift is empirical, and it is not even one number -- land gradient rises 1.408x at the median and 1.695x at p99 between the 2.5M and 10M builds. No single factor or exponent removes it. The exported field moves with it: scarp_potential above zero goes 0.2822 to 0.3410 of land, above 0.25 goes 0.0506 to 0.0949, mean where non-zero 0.1247 to 0.1924.

A NORMALISED FORM TRANSPORTS AND A RANK FORM IS NOT NEEDED. Bar declared before the runs at 1.15x on every quantile p50-p99, baseline declared at 30 km. Relief below the MEAN land elevation within 30 km, over 30 km: 0.909, 0.932, 1.046, 1.134 at p75-p99, inside the bar; its p50 is structurally zero because the measure is one-sided, which leaves the bar undefined rather than missed. Relief below the MINIMUM within the same ball fails (1.285, 1.053, 1.110, 1.206, 1.247) and the reason is worth keeping: a minimum is an extreme-value statistic biased by how many cells the ball holds, and the fine mesh holds three times as many.

TWO DEFECTS FIXED, both unambiguous. (1) The numerator differenced r_elevation, the generator's shaping parameter, against a denominator in km, so it was not a rise over a run at all: dh/de = 120e^3(1-e) is zero at sea level, peaks near 12.7 km/unit at e=0.75 and returns to zero at the ceiling, and the coded and physical distributions differ by 7x at p99. It also ignored the 1/g relief scaling, so the same terrain scarped identically at any gravity. Now converts through scaledHeightKm and pipeline.js passes reliefScale. (2) The neighbour filter was r_elevation[nb] <= 0, an elevation-sign test inside a function whose own land test is surface_class -- CLAUDE.md rule 1. It discarded every downhill neighbour on a dry closed-basin floor below sea level: 5.3 per cent of land at 2.5M and 8.6 at 10M, four fifths endorheic. THE SPREAD IS ON THE TEMPERATURE AXIS, which is neither where this row nor where section 31 expected it. All three schemes separate multiplicatively into a power law in runoff and an exponential in temperature, so d lnW/dT = n*gamma + 1/T_e and only n and T_e belong to the scheme. Holding one axis at a time: runoff exponent alone 1.04x to 1.19x across the sweep, temperature e-folding alone 1.49x down to 1.35x, crossing nowhere.

Section 31's 'about 30 per cent weaker under GKWM' compared only the runoff-driven INCREMENT and left out the temperature term, which is the larger part of the derivative at every gamma in the sweep. That framing is corrected in section 17d rather than repeated.

THE TEMPERATURE AXIS WAS INVISIBLE BECAUSE pedogenesis.yaml MIS-STATED ITS OWN EQUIVALENCE. It justified temperature_e_folding_k 13.7 as 'an activation energy near 74 kJ/mol at 288 K'. The linearised Arrhenius is T_e = R*T0^2/E_a, so 13.7 K is 50.3 kJ/mol and 74 kJ/mol is 9.3 K -- and 74.0 is exactly rokgem's par_E_a default, giving 8.912 K at its par_ref_T0 of 8.4777 C. The comment made two schemes that differ by 1.47x on the temperature term look like they agreed. Value PRESERVED at 13.7; only the justification is corrected.

CLASS MAPPING DONE, and it is declared rather than assumed because under GKWM it is inseparable from the exponent: reassigning a clastic class between shale and sand moves the effective exponent between 0.68 and 0.74 with no change of scheme. A source exists and it is Stark and Firestone (1995), now fetched, read and registered: references/stark1995-mechanisms-for-soil-moisture-effects-on-nitrifying-bacteria.pdf. It measures nitrification against soil WATER POTENTIAL in a silt loam, in two treatments that separate the two mechanisms -- shaken slurries with NH4 in excess, so only cell dehydration acts, fitting k = 15.4*exp(0.58*psi) with r2 0.958, and moist soil, where substrate diffusion acts too.

The axis problem that defeated Greaves and Carter does not arise, because this model already carries a potential axis and nothing has to be relabelled. SoilInput::get_mineral builds wilting point and field capacity by inverting Cosby (1984) eqn 1 at heads of 10^4.2 and 10^2.0 cm, which are -1.554 and -0.0098 MPa, and Soil::wfps is (wcont*gawc + gwp)/gwsats, which is Theta/Theta_s exactly. So Cosby eqn 1 makes potential a power law in water-filled pore space, per gridcell, out of the sand and clay the model already reads.

Placed there and anchored where they anchor, at -0.1 MPa: their moist soil falls to 0.510 at -0.5 MPa and 0.333 at this model's wilting point; the limb gives a median 0.526 (IQR 0.519-0.619) and 0.364 (IQR 0.356-0.424) over the current soil map's 4105 gridcells. The bracket is 0.333 to 0.430, the two treatments, and the limb is inside it near the moist-soil end, which is the end it should be at: the operator has no other term for substrate diffusion and substrate_partition's aerobic share GROWS as the soil dries.

ALSO SETTLED, and it narrows the question permanently: base 3 and rate 5 are ONE number. The limb is exp(5*log(3)*(w-0.6)), a slope of 5.493 per unit WFPS written as two factors, so any pair with the same product is the same limb and no measurement can separate them. There is no second source to look for.

Found while doing it and filed separately: get_mineral inverts Cosby's heads as if gravity were Earth's, world-slpa. It moves both sides of this comparison together, so it does not invalidate it, but it is what the comparison rests on.

Measured, and there is no crossing. The bucket floor in landmod's land water step is unreachable in exact arithmetic: fluxmod's humidity solve takes AMAX1 against the level humidity so the surface evaporation never adds water, the line below it caps that same withdrawal at the store divided by the timestep on every land cell whatever the snowpack holds, and every other contribution to the surface flux adds because rainmod builds the snowfall rate as a subset of the total precipitation rate. The snow-exhaustion path this issue named is the wrong suspect: the cap is unconditional, so a snowpack absorbs part of a withdrawal already limited against the soil store and leaves the store fuller than bare ground would, not emptier. Same conclusion for the layered column, where negatives originate only in the top layer and cascade downward, so a column total at or above zero leaves every layer at or above zero. What survives is the rounding of an exactly cancelling difference. land_water_ledger.py:bucket_floor_bound sweeps the chain in the model's own real kind over 27,952,428 combinations, 537,264 of them with the cap binding and 1,965,203 with the snowpack exhausted, and the worst crossing is 2.78e-17 m of water: 1.54e-2 kg on the largest T21 land cell in one timestep, and 6.38e4 kg over a whole orbit if every land cell clipped at every step, which is 1.2e-12 of the land soil water stock. Two falsification arms remove one closing property each and both produce a macroscopic crossing (85.6 mm and 5.4 mm), so the bound is a measurement and not a null result. The term is out of the ledger graph and into absences with the bound; unowned_source stays because it is the destination the boundary_receives_from_inside mutation is built on. landcolumn.f90's comments now say the floor is unreachable and why. No accumulator, no restart record and no ledger term were needed. Commit 919f02d2.

NOT A DEFECT on this world, bounded. The remainder form is Parton et al. (1993) eqn 10 p. 788, unguarded in the source too, and under that paper's own eqn 8 leaching coefficients (0.01 + 0.04*sand, saturating at 18 cm H2O/month) the remainder is positive over the whole texture simplex, bottoming out at +0.097 at pure sand. The CENTURY 5 update the code applies instead (0.03 + 0.12*sand at 1.9 cm/month) is what admits -0.003, and it arrived with the LPJ-GUESS subtree, so it is upstream and not a divergence this project made. Reversing needs clay+silt below 0.0039 (sand above 0.996) AND percolation at 0.98 of the leaching saturation point, both at once. No input path in the model reaches it: the soil map's sandiest cell is 0.663 sand with a worst remainder of 0.263 over 1019 land cells; soilinput.h's coarse LPJ soil code, the sandiest texture the model can be handed at 0.90 sand, still leaves 0.0754; the fixed-texture fallback leaves 0.569. No clamp applied and no coefficient changed. mineral_reactivity.yaml now registers the reachability boundaries, the soil code minimum and the source-coefficient variant, all checked by the gate with three new fixtures. One adjacent path filed as world-sptx: somfluxes mixes peat and mineral texture, which drops the coarse-code remainder to 0.009, unreachable while run_peatland is 0. Read from source and from the soil map; nothing execution-verified, LPJ-GUESS does not build on this tree.

Three kinds. The mask is not what makes the argument safe: SQRT(273./dt) under where(losun), SQRT of a sum of squares, ALOG(ztau0) which is clamped unconditionally above the where. And the mask was the guard over a value never written: swr's cloud-optics chain and its aerosol two-stream each write a scratch array and read it on the next line, so an excluded lane read stack contents; both are preset now, which is invisible on a kept lane because each is stored before it is read on the same pass. Two premises had moved. The set_source_files_properties block was already gone from plasim/CMakeLists.txt (b30e314e, when the profile went to -O2), so rainmod already compiles vectorised. And ra4 is no longer one number: world-ako split the Magnus-Teten coefficients by phase, so ra4s returns the liquid 35.86 K only for pt >= tmelt, where pt - ra4 is at least 237.3 K. The liquid pole is therefore unreachable and only the ice pole at 7.65 K is live. The exponent clamps rainmod already carried do not reach either: they bound exp(), not the division that forms the exponent, and a divisor at zero traps on -ffpe-trap=zero before the clamp applies. ra4d(pt,ppole) = max(pt - ppole, 1.0) in plasimmod is one definition of the floor; the pole is an argument rather than taken from pt, because fluxmod and seamod select the phase from the arm they are in and not from the temperature, and a function that chose it would let a site disagree with its own latent heat. 47 divisors floored: 40 rainmod, 2 fluxmod, 2 seamod, 2 landmod, 1 simba. Every (TMELT - ra4s(X)) numerator left alone, being a constant and not a pole. The floor binds below 8.65 K on the ice side and 36.86 K on the liquid side, where the exponent is about -4700 and exp of it underflows, so no value the model keeps moves. T21 production binary builds and links. The probe half is world-v9j9.

SO THE HYPERDIFFUSION DOES MOVE THIS SPECTRUM, by more than the whole of filter_kappa is worth (0.196 dex at the same wavenumber). The section 'The hyperdiffusion is not what damps this model' in exoplasim/notes/resolution-tuned-parameters.md is rewritten, not marked.

WHY THE ORIGINAL READ AS A NULL, both halves. The arms differed at one level in ten; and the comparison that made the filter look dominant was computed from a rate law that exoplasim/notes/filter-spectral-price.md refutes with two timestep pairs, at gamma 8 where the model runs gamma 16. Even on its own terms that table is a gamma 8 table: the filter's margin over the hyperdiffusion at half the truncation falls from 1632x to 6.4x on the move to gamma 16.

The standalone re-run the issue specified is not needed and is not blocked -- the arms it wanted already exist, at T21 rather than T42, and answer it more strongly. Nothing here is calibrated against stability_probe.json (world-qnue).

The spectral half is MEASURED and the acceptance criterion is answered by refutation: the confinement criterion cannot choose kappa, at any rung, and that is measured rather than argued.

THE RATE LAW THE WHOLE ROW RESTED ON IS REFUTED. legmod.f90 folds the filter into every per-mode transform WEIGHT, and what passes through those weights is the nonlinear TENDENCY -- no filtered value is ever stored back into the prognostic spectral state. So the filter attenuates the source that fills a wavenumber by a fixed factor rather than damping the state at a rate, and its spectral effect carries no timestep. Two pairs differing in MPSTEP alone, same binary by sha, same cold start, same seed:

  T21 gamma 16, dt 45 -> 22.5: depth at 0.8N moves +0.009 dex, 0.1 sigma; rate law predicts -0.296 against a three-sigma bar of 0.15
  T42 gamma 16, dt 45 -> 30:   depth moves -0.007 dex, 0.2 sigma; predicted -0.169 against a bar of 0.08

The bite point does not move at either rung. So '2*kappa*(n/N)^gamma/dt, an e-folding every 169 seconds at the truncation, 450x to 1600x the hyperdiffusion' is not a rate the spectrum obeys, and the comparison it licensed is between a rate on the state and a thing that is not one.

THE SURVIVING LAW, exp(-2 kappa x^gamma), is confirmed on the gamma pair: T42 dt 30, gamma 8 vs 16, differing in NFILTEREXP alone, 12 two-orbit windows each. Depth at 0.8N moves +0.789 +/- 0.036 dex at 22 sigma where f^2 predicts +0.970 and the rate law +0.763; the sharper test is the gamma 8 bite point, where the two laws disagree by nearly a factor of two -- f^2 says 0.675, the rate law says 0.381, it measures 0.688.

WHAT KAPPA COSTS, measured. The whole of kappa 8 is worth 0.196 dex of depletion at 0.8 of the truncation, against a total measured depletion of 0.602 dex at T42 and 0.969 to 1.418 at T21. So the filter is a third of it at T42 and a fifth at T21; the hyperdiffusion and the spectrum's own steepening carry the rest, and world-ba0 measures the hyperdiffusion's share at 0.449 dex.

WHY NO KAPPA SWEEP WAS RUN. The confinement criterion goes as kappa^(-1/gamma) = kappa^(-1/16), so a factor of two in kappa moves the bite point by 0.030 of the truncation -- below the instrument's quantisation at T21 (1/21 = 0.048) and at it at T42 (1/42 = 0.024) against a measured three-sigma bar of 0.000 to 0.021. The acceptance criterion 'a kappa chosen against the spectral confinement criterion at each rung' is not achievable at the gamma the model runs. The depth at 0.8N can see a factor of two, at about 1.5 bars at T42 and below the bar at T21 -- so a sweep would price kappa, not choose it, and the price is already known analytically from a law now checked on two independent contrasts.

Counting ga7's real k-terms out of the SOCRATES spectral files against radmod's own loop structure, the band-resolved candidate's transcendental work is 6,800 to 26,800 instructions per cell per radiation call against the present scheme's 37,400 to 84,900 -- cheaper at every corner of both brackets, because the broadband scheme is quadratic in levels where a k-term scheme is linear, and its kernel is a scalar masked pow at 116 instructions where the candidate's is a vectorisable exp at 5.1. So the swap is not refused on cost and the fallback optimisation would be work thrown away, which is what this row exists to prevent. The fallbacks are priced anyway: the exp/log identity returns 17 percent (93 against 112 instructions) and is less accurate; removing the where masks returns 7.6x on the kernel but is not bit-identical and is filed as world-43rk. The scheme decision itself stays with clim-61, which now needs only a cost per timestep on a quiet machine.

DECIDED, and the decision is that it is three quantities wearing one name. (1) A closed BASIN's inundated area through the year is HYDROGRAPHY's, and it needs no curve, model or preprocessor this project does not already have: basins.nc carries level/area/volume at 128 levels, the coupling matrix already crosses a per-basin quantity to the grid, the climatology carries time bins with lib/climatology.py owning their weights, and carve_verdict.penman_open_water already integrates the diurnal cycle for the same Jensen reason so a bin is not a new kind of evaluation. The cost is that surface_water.py integrates basin storage through those bins instead of over annual_mean and its convergence criterion becomes a PERIODIC steady state where the year closes on itself -- a new criterion, not a new solver -- plus LSHY-6 lowering the annual interval_floor on open_water_evaporation and surface_runoff, which a sub-annual balance may not book against and which is annual because the producer is annual and ExoPlaSim cannot evaporate routed water at all. The size is set by residence time, so the honest product is a per-basin seasonal amplitude carried by the low-capacity basins. Filed as world-15i0. (2) A FLOODPLAIN's is a routing cell's, needs a HAND CDF and a routing model neither of which exists here, and SHOULD NOT HAVE AN OWNER YET; external-model-survey.md section 52a already records that the basin curves are a different quantity sharing the word. (3) A seasonally saturated SOIL is not an inundated area: ExoPlaSim's land column and LPJ-GUESS's soil column both carry a water CONTENT and neither carries an area, and turning one into the other is a saturated-fraction closure, which world-n9sd withdrew. Naming them as candidates was a category error rather than a shortlist. So wet-2, wet-8 and wet-10 each have to say which of the three they need; a methane ledger treating 'seasonally inundated' as one class would book two supports and a category error into one number. Recorded in hydrography/notes/land-water-ledger.md and hydrography/config/wetness.yaml.

EXPLORATION delivered in notes/audits/snow-albedo-zenith.md with analysis/snow_albedo_zenith.py behind it, registered in config/pipeline.yaml. Form: alpha(mu0) = alpha_diffuse ** K(mu0) with van de Hulst's escape function K = (3/7)(1+2 mu0), which has NO fitted coefficient and whose normalisation puts K(2/3)=1, so a scheme with no zenith angle is quoting the mu0=2/3 value. alpha_diffuse comes per band from the model's own star-weighted dsnowalb*, so ClimaLand's Earth coefficients are not inherited. Sized: zenith span 0.186 on cold snow and 0.364 on warm, against the temperature ramp's entire broadband range of 0.375; an independent snow spectrum gives 0.208 on this star against 0.150 on a solar Planck, so the redder star makes the term LARGER. Priced: sign flips with latitude, polar-cap annual mean -6.3 to -9.0 W/m2 per unit snow area, global -0.14 K at 2 per cent snow cover to -1.35 K at 20 per cent, bracketed because no climatology exists and declared an upper bound in two named ways. Verdict on radmod's ocean formula: WRONG FORM, RIGHT LOCATION -- Fresnel replaces the albedo rather than acting on it, saturates at 0.15 and carries no surface property, but radmod:swr is the only place zmu0 and the surface albedo are both in scope. No model change made.

THE RESULT THAT WAS NOT ANTICIPATED. The two instruments disagree by a third at T85: 28.1x T21 per orbit in instructions, 36.6x in wall and 37.3x in model CPU. On the bed all three rungs retire within five per cent of each other per CPU-second; in a production run T85 retires 3.85e9 against T21's 5.11e9. FIXED, commit 9916bd4c on fanout-X2, with the issue's premise about the fault site CORRECTED. WHAT THE MODEL REFUSES. The SIGFPE is at radmod.f90's SQRT(273./dt(:,jlev)) and dt(NHOR,NLEP) is the gridpoint TEMPERATURE field (plasimmod.f90:677), not the timestep -- that expression reduces the water-vapour amount to a standard temperature. So the model is refusing a NON-POSITIVE GRIDPOINT TEMPERATURE at the first radiation call, which is the same signature as world-td3's death at -12.81 K, and nothing at that site reads a step. The site therefore carries no evidence for a timestep mechanism at all, and the issue's reading of it as one is what made the timestep look like the discriminant. DOES THE ROUTE WALK INTO IT? No, and by construction. sequencing.md section D changes the rung and the step alternately -- T21 at 45, reconverge T21 at 30, convert to T42 at 30, reconverge T42 at 22.5, convert to T85 at 22.5 -- so every change of rung on the route happens at CONSTANT dt. Both conversions in this issue (45 to 22.5 and 30 to 22.5) are off-route; they were taken for the arm-A-versus-arm-B comparison whose consumer SPAT-8's closure removed. lib/rungs._check_route asserts the alternation at import, so the invariant is a check with a right answer rather than a description. WHAT IS ENFORCED. The converter's contract has required equal timestep since v1 and nothing looked. Two consequences are arithmetic rather than conjecture: nstep is COPY policy and elapsed time is nstep*dt, so the calendar and the stellar cycle (which restart_schema's own nstep policy says take their phase from that count, and which it says is 'sound only because v1 requires equal timesteps') move by the ratio -- a factor of 0.5 for the 45-to-22.5 case; and the two stored leapfrog levels are a derivative over the donor's step read by the target as spanning its own. check_timestep now refuses, before a byte is written, and states in its own docstring that it does NOT claim to be the cause of the SIGFPE. The step is not in the restart, so it arrives from --source-timestep-minutes/--target-timestep-minutes or from --source-manifest/--target-manifest; --timestep-unchecked is the explicit arm and records itself in the report, which gains a 'timestep' block so 'checked and equal' and 'not checked' are distinguishable. THE TEST, and a note on the acceptance criterion. The self-test refuses BOTH of this issue's conversions, on the contract rather than on which one trapped. The criterion asked for a test that fails on the bad donor and passes on the good one, and the evidence does not support calling the 45-to-22.5 case good: it ran 900 steps, which is about a seventh of an orbit and is exactly the length exoplasim/notes/physics-filter-stability.md says qualifies a state against refusal and nothing else. Treating it as a pass would be the same instrument error the note warns about. The positive arm is instead the route itself: the self-test walks rungs.ESCALATION_ROUTE and requires every rung change on it to be ACCEPTED, so the check cannot be satisfied by refusing everything. That needs a run and this host is contended, so no arm of it was attempted. It is now unblocking rather than blocking: the ladder's T42 rung runs at dt 30 on the declared route and converts to T85 at dt 30's own reconvergence, so no route conversion needs the answer.

FIXED, and the acceptance procedure was re-derived because the runs it names are not on this machine. run_8044646ea7f0 and the T42 arms are absent, so no --through sweep was possible; the question the sweep was to answer is answerable in closed form and the answer is now computed rather than swept.

WHAT THE FLAPPING WAS. On a settled run the exponential fit has nothing to grip and the fallback tests |offset| + half_width, where offset is slope * tau_expected and half_width carried 100 per cent of the offset. Both terms are the same slope error multiplied by the same relaxation time of about ten orbits, so the statistic compared with the 0.15 K allowance has about twice the offset's scale. var(slope) = scatter^2 * tau * 12 / (n(n^2-1)), so at the T21 baseline's stationary scatter of 0.07 K and a lag-1 of 0.615 the statistic's standard error at a ten-orbit window EXCEEDS its own threshold. That is the wander from 0.031 to 0.255 and the seven flips, and no widening chosen by sweep would have explained it.

THE WINDOW. Against the declared bar that a threshold discriminates only when its statistic's standard error is at most a third of it, the window is 35 orbits. Bracket: 21 if consecutive orbits were independent, 34.1 at the measured lag-1, 43.9 at a lag-1 of 0.8. The factor tau is exactly what the model's memory costs. assess_convergence.DEFAULT_WINDOW_ORBITS is computed from three inputs each with a citation, not typed, and every assessment reports resolving_power.window_orbits_for_offset_criterion from THAT run's own scatter and autocorrelation, so the number follows the resolution up the ladder instead of being a T21 constant carried to T170. Where tau had to come from inside the window it is labelled a lower bound.
