Not needed. The ocean-transport loop computes the term this row approximates, and it runs the way every other loop in this project runs -- so there is no window in which a declared-gradient q-flux is the best available answer.

The row's instrument was a residual: prescribe a sea surface temperature, diagnose the heat flux that holds it, apply that as a correction. On Earth that means something because the prescribed SST is OBSERVED, so the residual reads as the transport that must exist given the real surface. Vesper has no observed SST, so any prescribed field is a choice and the residual measures the choice. The best version of it -- a declared gradient reduction, magnitude declared and sensitivity measured -- returns d(climate)/d(assumed transport), which the ocean loop supersedes by returning a transport from a model.

OCN-5 had already named this row's central trap one level up, and in almost the same words: an ocean model forced by a climatology a zero-transport slab produced, and restored toward that climatology's own SST, returns a transport of zero by construction. Its escape is flux forcing with no temperature restoring and weak salinity restoring only as an explicit control. That is the same circularity that makes prescribing the free slab's own climatology useless here, so the two rows were solving one problem at two levels and OCN-5 states it first and better.

WHAT SURVIVES AND WHERE. No-q-flux stays a DECLARED STRUCTURAL TERM in the error budget until the ocean loop supplies a computed one; CLIM-16 settled that horizontal diffusion stays off and that a constant diffusivity is a bound on the missing transport rather than the transport, and that stands untouched. Two costs measured while closing this are recorded on OCN-5 rather than lost: yfsst is (NHOR,14), per cell and per bin, so any diagnosed correction is resolution-specific and does not transfer between rungs without regridding; and an arm that USES such a field costs a full commissioning, not the single prescribed-SST run this description implied -- the prescribed segment is cheap because a prescribed surface has no mixed layer to equilibrate.

The code is not lost either and needs no row to protect it: oceanmod already carries both halves, nocean = 0 diagnosing yfsst2 and writing code 903, and nfluko = 1 reading the same code back and aborting by name when it is absent. If a q-flux is ever wanted the machinery is there and verified end to end.

THE WEIBULL SHAPE, the issue's second term, was a real defect of the same shape. The check read subgrid_wind.weibull_shape, which is THIS WORLD's and is refitted at build time from a high-cadence extract, so a Vesper refit would have moved an Earth verdict for a Vesper reason. It now reads its own earth_check.weibull_shape, sourced to Monahan (2006) Part I section 5, which asks exactly this question of QuikSCAT and answers that the Rayleigh PDF -- Weibull shape 2 -- is a reasonable approximation to the GLOBAL POOLED PDF of ocean wind speed. The pooled PDF is the right object because the check applies one moment ratio to one global mean production; the same paper's Fig. 3 shows the LOCAL shape running 2 to 6, which is why a typical local value would have been the wrong number. The window rule is a span of about twenty times tau after the approach, measured against lib/autocorrelation.py on synthetic series with tau known in closed form, criteria fixed first: batch means reach the coverage criterion there, batches of two tau miss it however many there are, and estimating tau inside the same span covers worse at every length. Fixing tau itself needs about 290 to 480 times tau, of order a thousand orbits at equilibrium, so it is not a target this project can design against and the recommendation is reported as a bracket. Written up in exoplasim/notes/convergence-lengths.md, which also supersedes its own earlier ten-times-tau figure. The sibling arithmetic that put this at seventeen independent samples and seventy orbits conflated n_eff with n; the relation gives about seventeen orbits, and it is the wrong question anyway because the 0.210 K spread it was fitted to is contaminated by the approach. Consuming the rule when a run is specified rather than after it is spent is world-cikl.

THE RANGE. Fig. 1's axes are 10 to 10,000 g m-2 over eight standard terrestrial cloud models; the tuned tables span tau_N 1 to 500, which inverts to about 7 to 14,000 g m-2; p. 2130 calls 10 to 1000 typical of observed stratiform cloud.

WHERE THIS MODEL SITS, and it is answerable with no climatology because the surface pressure cancels out of zlwp: zlwp(j) = 1000 clwref gascon T(j) (dsigma(j)/sigma(j)) exp(-z(j)/hl) / ga. On the ten-level quartic grid at a 50 hPa top the bottom three layers carry 43 to 105 g m-2 across column water 10 to 50 kg m-2, inside the range; layers above sigma 0.55 carry under 30 and the top three under 2.2 at every column water a moist column reaches. So the low cloud is inside the fit and the high cloud is one to three decades below it, in the regime the 1984 paper excludes by name at p. 690. radmod's own min(1000,...) cap lands on the top of the typical range at tau 145, inside the tuned table, so the ceiling is safe and the floor is not.

THE EFFECTIVE RADIUS IS A SCHEME BOUNDARY TO DECLARE, not a gap to fill, and the declaration is now in docs/src/reference/design-intent.md. Stephens Eq. Supplying r_e means replacing Stephens with Slingo, which is a scheme decision.

clwref DOES NOT MOVE, and that is falsifiable rather than preferred. FIXED. The cause is not -g. gfortran stores the source path of every I/O statement in .rodata for its runtime diagnostics; that string survives with no debug flags at all, and the path reaches it through the cpp line markers CMake's preprocess-and-scan writes, which gcc(1) states -ffile-prefix-map does not remap ('Directories referenced by directives are not affected'). Measured: 343 such lines carried the build root. CMake's Ninja generator always hands the compiler an absolute source path (verified for a source dir inside the bin dir and for a generated file in the bin dir), and its Fortran preprocess rule carries no launcher hook, so no flag and no generator arrangement reaches it.

exoplasim/scripts/prefix_map_launcher.py applies the -ffile-prefix-map options ALREADY on the compile line to those markers, registered by build_model.py as CMAKE_Fortran_COMPILER_LAUNCHER. plasim/CMakeLists.txt keeps the declaration: the binary-directory map lost its trailing slash so it now reaches DW_AT_comp_dir, and the SHTns prefix is mapped because the include's path reaches the line table.

T21 l10 p16 production is 599021395fd30d3c from both. Negative control, same source and same CMakeLists with the launcher removed: ef1de3eb99b44e43 against 3d88e3c121622de1. No absolute path remains in the executable and the runtime diagnostics now name the bare source file.

rebuild_binaries.py stamps build_inputs (the shas of plasim/CMakeLists.txt and the launcher) because both change every executable and nothing hashed either; assert_launcher_registered() reads the wiring back out of build_model.py.

FIXED. The guard is not loosened and there is no flag; what is added is a way to declare a REMOVAL in advance so the guard can distinguish it from a value change.

lib/provenance.py:REMOVED_CONFIG_KEYS takes the shape of the fork's mainline_divergences files, which is the precedent that has held: the values the key held are recorded verbatim beside the removal, and the gate checks BOTH halves -- the key must be gone from config/planet.yaml, and the artifact's recorded value must be one the declaration names. A run whose manifest holds any other value had the key's VALUE move under it before the key went; that is real drift and is still refused. An undeclared removal is still drift. An ADDED key is still drift, because an added key can be read; the tool for a declarative addition is the consumer's inert set. A rename is therefore half declarable and half refused, which is correct while the new name is read.

Making the declaration is deliberate and recorded: it cannot be written without reading what the config held, it carries the issue that removed the key, the paths the meaning moved to and a written argument for why the removal cannot change what a run integrated, and it lives in git rather than on a command line.

removal_problems() is the honesty check and check_consistency runs it as a row of its own, not only under --self-test. It fails on a declaration the tree no longer bears out: the key back in the config, a moved_to path that is not there, or the key's name appearing in any Python source outside where it moved. That last is the answer to 'what evidence establishes no reader' and it is stated for what it is -- a TEXTUAL trace with the same blind spot SURFACE_UNREAD_MODEL_KEYS records, which is why the written argument is the other half and is not optional. The AST route was not needed to close this: the mechanical half only has to keep the declaration honest, not to establish the claim on its own.

A resume that rests on a declaration prints it. Six self-test cases with their controls; 25 cases 0 failed. Verified against run_ade7373b4c90, whose manifest holds the removed table: the removal applies and the run's real drift, model.timestep_minutes 45.0 -> 30.0, is still refused.

The procedural alternative (freeze config while a commissioning is in flight) is not adopted for removals and is not needed for them. It remains the only answer for a key whose value changes, which is what the guard exists to catch.

THE THREE FIVES ARE ECHAM'S RE-FIT, NOT LOUIS'S, which is exactly what this issue asked. Louis fits F = 1 - b Ri/(1 + c sqrt(|Ri|)) unstable and F = 1/(1 + b' Ri)^2 stable, with b = 2b' = 9.4 chosen so dF/dRi is continuous across neutrality -- a constraint, not a fit. His c is not a constant: c = C* a^2 b sqrt(z/z0) with C* = 7.4 momentum and 5.3 heat. The model's b=c=d=5 with 2b and 3b folded in corresponds to Louis's b near 10 and 15 against his 9.4. And no replacement follows from the primary: Louis states his own values 'are rather uncertain because of the large scatter in the observations'. Disposition IRREDUCIBLE, now checked rather than asserted.

PART (a) IS REFUTED AS PROPOSED. 160 m is not Louis's either -- his eq. 22 is Blackadar's form, he calls lambda 'an adjustable parameter' and took it as 100 m. Nothing in Blackadar's or Louis's form makes lambda proportional to a scale height, so scaling 160 m by 0.766 the way clwhsc was scaled has nothing under it and is NOT done. clwhsc's scaling worked because the quantity was a geometric height in a formula whose neighbours already scaled as 1/g; lambda is not that. What transfers is Blackadar (1962), where lambda follows from the geostrophic wind and the Coriolis parameter. Not held. Fetching it is world-80ia.

ARTEFACT OF THE SHAPE FUNCTION'S DOMAIN, not a physical ceiling, established by reading the curve rather than by argument.

s(t) = t^4(5-4t) is a Hermite interpolant whose four defining conditions are all endpoint conditions on [0,1]: s(0)=s'(0)=s''(0)=0 for the flatlands, s(1)=1 with s'(1)=0 for the peak compression. s' is negative above 1, so the polynomial turns over, reaches zero at t=1.25 and goes below sea level beyond, and Math.min(elev,1) was the guard against that inversion. The codebase already names [0,1] as the domain: applyDetailNoise refuses to invert the same polynomial at elev >= 0.99. The physical ceiling on relief exists and is a separate object, scaledHeightKm's 1/g out of sigma/(rho g), applied after this curve.

FIXED with a branch above the domain, s(t) := t, giving RELIEF_KM_PER_UNIT * elev. Continuous at the join where s(1)=1 already, gradient equal to the curve's own mean gradient across its domain, strictly increasing everywhere, no constant the curve did not already have, bit-identical below 1, and applied before reliefScale so selection stays gravity-invariant.

FOUR REASONS, all properties of the two codebases. It integrates the local surface mass balance alone, dH/dt = b, where a glacier's thickness solves continuity with a flux divergence -- and glaciermod's own header says it is a coupling slot for an external model that SETS the height. It is zero by construction over the ablation zone and trunk, which is where a glacier erodes, and largest at the accumulation summit where a real sheet is nearest stagnant, so it is ANTI-CORRELATED with the wanted field rather than a noisy estimate of it. It cannot decide the exponent, which is the whole width of the bracket: a thickness carrying no ice dynamics does not measure the thickness-versus-flux choice, it imposes the thickness-fixed limb, so the bracket would look collapsed while having been settled by an artefact of the coupling -- worse than the honest bracket. And it is a cell mean against a law quartic in H: u ~ H^4, q ~ H^5, and <H>^4 is not <H^4>.

Kessler's own caveats travel with the form: the single-drop fit is good to about 40 per cent, a constant N0 misrepresents evaporation because the process depletes small drops preferentially, and the rate is for standard air density.

THE NLAT TERM GOES ON THE WIDTH. rcrit encodes the subgrid humidity distribution's width, and cloud onset sits a distance proportional to that width below saturation. Specific humidity is a passive scalar, so Kolmogorov-Obukhov-Corrsin gives variance proportional to L^(2/3), hence sigma as L^(1/3), and a cell's width goes as 1/NLAT: 1-rcrit = (1-rcrit_T21)*(32/NLAT)^(1/3). Keyed by a new rcritwidth, derived from NLAT unless given a positive value, with rcritmod and rcritslope keeping their existing meanings on top as the sweep handles.

RCRITMOD IS THE WRONG OPERATOR AND WAS NOT USED, which is worth recording because it is the obvious choice: it MULTIPLIES rcrit, and the factor that gives the right floor at T85 drives the sigma limb's end levels past 1.0, where (rh-rcrit)/(1-rcrit) divides by zero. Width scaling is bounded below 1 by construction.

The floor goes 0.85 to 0.869, 0.881, 0.896 and 0.906 at T31, T42, T63 and T85, and 1/(1-rcrit)^2 -- the lever this row prices -- from 44 to 58, 71, 92 and 112. T21 is bit-identical BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by arithmetic: the unit factor is SKIPPED rather than applied, because 1-(1-x) is not a float identity for every x.

ZCCA AND ZCCB DO NOT TAKE THIS SCALING and stay irreducible for a different reason, argued at the value: their exponent is set by an unresolved convective area fraction the scheme does not carry, so no exponent between the L^-2 diluting limit and the cell-filling limit is derivable from what is there. A tuning that is a declared function of the grid can be tested against the grid; one whose exponent is unknowable cannot, and saying which is which is the honest state.

FIXED, and the row's mechanism was half wrong. It was right about zcnow and wrong about what advances sd: plasimmod.f90:assoc_spectral points each thread's sdp at a disjoint slice sd(mypid*NSPP+1 : +NSPP), and what carries sd from t to t+dt is step 4.b of spectrala writing THROUGH that pointer. mpsyncsp is an omp barrier and nothing else (mpimod_omp.f90:830); it publishes a write that has already happened. The old comment at plasim.f90:3776 attributed the advance to mpsyncsp and both notes repeated it; all three are corrected.

zcnow(:,:) = sd(:,:) at the head of the routine copies the WHOLE array into a thread-local allocatable while each thread owns one slice, and between that copy and 4.b there is no barrier. A thread held up in the copy reads slices other threads have already advanced, so its zcnow is a mixture of t and t+dt slice by slice. Terms 3 and 4 are the only ones reading it; terms 1, 2 and 5 come through mpgallsp and term 6 reads sd after mpsyncsp, which is exactly the seven-versus-two split observed.

THE FIX is one !$omp barrier immediately after the copy, inside the existing nenergy>1 .or. nconvtime>0 branch. Conditional is safe because both switches are broadcast by mpbci before this runs. No array added, so the 32 MB per-die target is untouched.

WHAT IT RESTS ON. Wood and Mason (1993) Eq. (33): the effective roughness of hilly ground is the length whose drag coefficient at the pressure scale height equals the SUM of the hills' pressure drag and the ground's skin friction, added in the DRAG COEFFICIENT. simba.f90:474 combines in quadrature in the LENGTH, which is the model's convention rather than the literature's, and the builder now follows the derivation. Beljaars et al. (2004) Eq. (6), Ca = 2*alpha*beta*Cmd*thetabar^2, QUADRATIC IN SUBGRID SLOPE rather than linear in relief amplitude, with their Eqs. (4) and (5) supplying h_m, l and alpha so none is assumed. Mason (1988): the cell average is of drag coefficients at the BLENDING HEIGHT, 27.3 m here against a lowest model level at 114.0 m, so the builder had been averaging an order of magnitude too high. Slope from Export.local_slope_deg, the mesh's own plane fit.

WHY THE OLD RELATION WAS STRUCTURALLY WRONG, which is the finding worth keeping: a coefficient multiplying an ELEVATION SPREAD has to carry the missing horizontal scale inside itself, and the horizontal scale of a within-cell spread IS THE CELL. That is why it drifted by a factor of 1.98 across the ladder.

DISPOSITION: derived, with a swept bracket on two attributions read out of the papers -- the wavelength attributed to the resolved slope (1 to 4 mesh spacings, entering only through logarithms) and WM93's two turbulence closures. Together they move the land mean by about 4 per cent.

WHERE THE DISTANCE FROM EARTH IS, checked rather than assumed: the two planets' COVER roughness agrees to within a fifth and neither is derived from the other, so the entire gap is the RELIEF term. Verified from the artifact: Earth's surface part 0.3162 m against this world's unrescaled 0.3751 m.

THE HYPOTHESIS IS REFUTED AT MATCHED WINDOW LENGTH. Over 41 orbits, the length the bare-rock arms were judged on, the vegetated baseline reads tau 1.46 against the bare-rock bootstrap's 1.82 -- the lake-bearing arm is the LESS autocorrelated of the two. The 5.49 that raised the question was the unsupported reading this row warned about in its own text, at an effective sample of 7.5.

WHAT IS TRUE INSTEAD is more useful and is why this closes rather than being re-scoped. Tau grows monotonically with the window it is measured on -- 1.00 at 20 orbits, 1.35 at 40, 1.90 at 60, 6.30 at 140 -- while the lag-1 correlation does not, sitting between 0.27 and 0.52 throughout. An AR(1) at the measured lag-1 would give 2.88 against the 6.30 measured on the same orbits, so the autocorrelation does not decay geometrically and tau is a property of the window rather than of the process. Batch means, which compute no tau at all, agree independently: the inflation over the independent expectation reaches 2.5 at a batch length of 20 and holds, which is tau 6.3 by an instrument that never estimates one.

AND THE QUANTITY TAU EXISTS TO CORRECT HAS ALREADY CONVERGED. The standard error of the mean is 0.0201 K at 20 orbits and 0.0255 at 140, while the independent expectation falls from 0.0201 to 0.0102. Seven times the orbits buy no better a mean. This model's per-orbit global mean surface temperature can be determined to about 0.025 K and no better, whatever is spent.

The follow-on is world-vd6a: PRODUCTION_SPAN_TAU_MULTIPLE prices the span through the one statistic that has already converged, and the rule does not close on a series whose tau depends on the window -- at 60 orbits it asks for 38 and at 140 for 126.

Resolved and committed. pedology emits an exchange complex -- pedogenesis.yaml's `exchange` block, build_soil.py:exchange_properties, and a `cec` column on the soil map -- and the ANUT-8 multiplier is a bound read off it. It collapsed to 54.09 set by magnesium, bracket 47.44 to 54.09, per-element K 31.15 / Ca 26.37 / Mg 54.09 / S 5.67, replacing a 1-to-5 bracket run at its upper end. It collapsed UPWARD: the old upper end was a base-depleted Hawaiian profile and this world's soils are base-saturated over most of the land, so ANUT-8 had been reporting a critical runoff an order of magnitude below its own construction. The verdict survives the capacity level, which is the one large exposure: the emitted level probe gives 19.6 and 27.3 at Dahlgren's halloysite endmembers, and the root term alone puts magnesium at 6.43 with no exchange complex in the arithmetic. Sources read for this: Sahrawat (1983) for the slopes, Solly et al. (2020) for the falsifiable organic-share check, the capacity envelope and the calcium share, Chadwick et al.
